title: On Dedicating the book to his old teacher
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：dedicate　|　正文 370 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dedicate 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the planner ① dedicated the book to his old teacher for the whole place, and every citizen in the district said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the planner ② dedicates the book to his old teacher without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ dedicate the book to his old teacher at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ dedicated the book to his old teacher before — a line in the report for March 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Dedicating the book to his old teacher for the whole place, the planner said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ dedicate a whole year to the work without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Dedicate a whole year to the work at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the report, and a new citizen from the next district ⑧ dedicates a whole year to the work for the whole place every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the square, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ dedicated the book to his old teacher again when nobody else would.

⑩ To dedicate the book to his old teacher, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the district remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the district forgets, somebody dedicates the book to his old teacher without a word of thanks again and somebody must dedicate the book to his old teacher for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 献给（一般过去式 dedicated the book to his old teacher：1949 年规划员头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 献给（一般现在 dedicates the book to his old teacher：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 献给（不定式 to dedicate the book to his old teacher：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 献给（过去完成时 had dedicated the book to his old teacher：1943 年三月的规划报告上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 献给（动名词 dedicating the book to his old teacher 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 把…专门用于（dedicate a whole year to the work：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去把…专门用于把整整一年扑在这件活上）
G. v. 把…专门用于（dedicate a whole year to the work：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 献给（后段两处：新来的市民照例 dedicates a whole year to the work，而母亲又一次 dedicated the book to his old teacher）

answers.why: dedicate 意为“献给”，1949 年规划员替所有人献给把那本书献给他的老先生，那是街区里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 dedicated。
dedicate 意为“献给”，自那以后规划员不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 dedicates。
dedicate 意为“献给”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯献给把那本书献给他的老先生”，此处为不定式 to dedicate the book to his old teacher。
dedicate 意为“献给”，规划报告里 三月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人献给过，故用过去完成时 had dedicated。
dedicate 意为“献给”，规划员说“献给把那本书献给他的老先生这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 dedicating the book to his old teacher 作主语。
dedicate 意为“把…专门用于”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去把…专门用于把整整一年扑在这件活上”，should ever 之后用原形 dedicate a whole year to the work。
dedicate 意为“把…专门用于”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻把…专门用于把整整一年扑在这件活上（dedicate a whole year to the work at once），以后再也不要提起。
dedicate 意为“献给”，新来的市民每个年份都照例把…专门用于把整整一年扑在这件活上，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 dedicates。
dedicate 意为“献给”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人献给把那本书献给他的老先生，用一般过去式 dedicated 叙述。
dedicate 意为“献给”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要献给把那本书献给他的老先生，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和街区记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dedicate 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the planner dedicated the book to his old teacher for the whole place, and nobody in the district forgot it.
Even now the planner dedicates the book to his old teacher without a word of thanks whenever the district asks.
Dedicating the book to his old teacher for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever dedicate a whole year to the work without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new citizen from the next district dedicates a whole year to the work for the whole place every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother dedicated the book to his old teacher again, and the district remembered that half.
